elements.quote: The proportion of people who will remain asymptomatic throughout the course of infection with severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), the cause of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), is not known. Studies that assess people at just one time point will overestimate the proportion of true asymptomatic infection...
elements.reason: The rationale section describes the current state of knowledge and key uncertainties, including the unknown proportion of asymptomatic infection and misclassification bias in single time-point studies.

elements.quote: The amount, and infectiousness, of asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection will determine what kind of measures will prevent transmission most effectively.
elements.reason: The importance and need for the review are explained in terms of its implications for choosing effective transmission-prevention measures.

elements.quote: The first two versions of the review have been published as preprints [7,8].
elements.reason: The manuscript cites previous versions of this living review (preprints [7,8]), and text_20 discusses other systematic reviews; however, the Introduction does not explicitly explain the need for the current review relative to those existing reviews/versions beyond the living-review framing.
This is a review of proportions of asymptomatic/presymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection and transmission, not a review of intervention effects, so no mechanism of action needs describing.
The review addresses observational and modelling evidence on infection and transmission proportions, not a complex intervention or delivery context, so a logic model is not required.

elements.quote: The objectives of this study were to address three questions: (1) Amongst people who become infected with SARS-CoV-2, what proportion do not experience symptoms at all during their infection? (2) Amongst people with SARS-CoV-2 infection who are asymptomatic when diagnosed, what proportion will develop symptoms later? (3) What proportion of SARS-CoV-2 transmission is accounted for by people who are either asymptomatic throughout infection or presymptomatic?
elements.reason: The Introduction explicitly states the study objectives as three clearly formulated review questions, satisfying the requirement for an explicit statement of objectives/questions.

elements.quote: The objectives of this study were to address three questions: (1) Amongst people who become infected with SARS-CoV-2, what proportion do not experience symptoms at all during their infection? (2) Amongst people with SARS-CoV-2 infection who are asymptomatic when diagnosed, what proportion will develop symptoms later? (3) What proportion of SARS-CoV-2 transmission is accounted for by people who are either asymptomatic throughout infection or presymptomatic?
elements.reason: This is a review of prevalence/proportion estimation rather than intervention effects, so PICO is not strictly required. The questions do specify population (people with SARS-CoV-2 infection) and outcomes (proportions asymptomatic, presymptomatic, transmission contribution), partially covering comparison elements, but no formal PICO framing or planned comparisons is provided.

elements.quote: Weincluded studies in any language of people with SARS-CoV-2 diagnosed by RT-PCR that documented follow-up and symptom status at the beginning and end of follow-up or investigated the contribution to SARS-CoV-2 transmission of asymptomatic or presymptomatic infection. We included contact-tracing investigations, case series, cohort studies, case-control studies, and statistical and mathematical modelling studies. We excluded the following study types: case reports of a single patient and case series in which participants were not enrolled consecutively.
elements.reason: Eligible designs, required follow-up and symptom-status documentation, and excluded study types are clearly specified; the three review question components are referenced via definitions in Box 1 (text_10).

elements.quote: Weincluded studies in any language... When multiple records included data from the same study population, we linked the records and extracted data from the most complete report.
elements.reason: Language eligibility is stated and preprints were evidently included (text_13), but no explicit dissemination year limits or formal publication-status criteria are reported in the eligibility criteria section.
The retrieved evidence does not distinguish exclusion because outcomes were not measured from exclusion because outcome results were not reported.

elements.quote: The reviewers determined which of the three review questions each study addressed, using the definitions in Box 1.
elements.reason: Studies are assigned to the three review questions, and synthesis groups are described (stratification by methods of identifying asymptomatic infection and setting in text_12), but the grouping criteria are only partially linked to the comparisons via Box 1 definitions not shown in the evidence.
Restrictions such as excluding single-patient case reports and non-consecutive case series are stated without any rationale for these restrictions.
